text:
Rickard Rakell is a 33-year-old scoring winger on a Penguins team that keeps losing, which makes him a trade candidate whether he likes it or not. Last week Yahoo Sports and NHLRumors.com relayed reports that he had blocked a deal to Chicago. Nothing in our facts confirms it, but his name is now on every list of Pittsburgh's possible moves, next to Erik Karlsson's.

The goals haven't stopped. He has five in his last ten games, six in 20 overall on 7.1 expected, and his goals have added more wins than all but 41 skaters in the league. What's missing is the setup work: five assists all season leaves him at 1.66 points per 60, below the range we'd expect from him (1.86 to 2.64). Pittsburgh's 5v5 share with him on the ice is a little over 51%.

Evolving-Hockey had him facing top-3% competition last season, a sign of how much the Penguins lean on him in hard minutes. Contenders looking for a finisher who can play up the lineup will keep calling. Whether he'll say yes is the question nobody outside the room can answer.
headline: Rakell keeps scoring while his name stays in play
